transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the weekly power-support allocation. We've got four portable power units — P-1, P-2, P-3, and P-4 — all listed as serviceable and available. They need to cover the clinic, communications shelter, battery shop, and refrigerated storage area for the coming week. I'd like each of you to walk through your area's needs and any concerns before I finalize the assignment and sign the support plan. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Ma'am, before we go further, I need to flag something. During yesterday's electrical inspection, I confirmed that P-2 is the only unit with the recently certified isolated-output transformer required by the clinic's sensitive diagnostic equipment. The certification entry is still pending on the base inventory board, so it hasn't shown up there yet, but P-2 needs to go to the clinic.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Ma'am, I need to flag something on the signal side. This morning I confirmed that the communications shelter's equipment requires regulated 28-volt output, which only P-4 provides. The updated compatibility note hasn't been added to the signal support annex yet, but P-4 needs to go to the communications shelter.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Ma'am, on the aviation-maintenance side, I need to flag something for the battery shop. I confirmed with the battery-shop supervisor that their charging rack requires P-1's approved connector and grounding lead. The shop's revised power worksheet hasn't been forwarded to the base planning cell yet, so that requirement isn't reflected in the current documentation. P-1 needs to go to the battery shop.
transcript.speaker: A4

I've confirmed that we're receiving a continuous-temperature shipment this coming week that requires P-3's 24-hour runtime capability. The receiving manifest hasn't been linked to the power-allocation request yet, so that requirement isn't reflected in the current documentation. P-3 needs to go to the refrigerated storage area.
